answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils by making reputation a cultivated trail, not a signup. Each identity must grow a vine of signed, epoch-stamped work that only lengthens when unaffiliated established peers countersign it. Cheap clones can appear in the meadow of new registrations, but they cannot collect emission until five such peers, over distinct epochs, walk that trail up a knoll of accumulated attestations. A swarm of lookalikes withers because no established agent will climb a knoll already thick with identical, same-day plots.
